learning_outcomes.text: Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Distinguish or classify what process engineering is and how it relates to product engineering.
Distinguish different production processes according to the degree of automation or the nature of the production flow.
Describe production processes using process diagrams, including their times.
Design and redesign single-product and multi-product production lines.
Design and redesign a workshop-based production system.
Minimize waste in a production process using lean manufacturing.
Efficient warehouse management based on costs and service level.
Distinguish types of production planning based on time horizon: sales and operations plan, master production schedule, and production scheduling.
Execute a company's sales and operations plan. Develop the master production schedule and material requirements planning, as well as capacity planning.
Develop very short-term production scheduling for the company using optimal and heuristic algorithms.
Understand and master the fundamental concepts of flexible manufacturing.
Understand the different types of production planning based on company typology.
Identify restrictions affecting proposed production sequences and know how to eliminate them.
Properly handle terms related to production planning.
Understand different industrial processes used in the manufacturing of everyday products.

syllabus_topics: Workshop-based or process-oriented production process design
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade is based on a written exam (70%), practical assignments (20%), and teamwork (10%). To pass, students must obtain at least 5 out of 10 in the written exam; otherwise, the final grade is the written exam score weighted out of 10. Students may opt for final assessment within 9 weeks, or renounce the call by not attending the final exam. Final assessment consists of a two-part exam, where both parts must be passed with at least 5 out of 10. For the extraordinary call, evaluation criteria are the same, and positive results from group work and computer practices in continuous assessment may be retained if the professor deems it appropriate.
